name: Biology Club
description: Explores biology beyond the classroom; often preps for competitions like the USA Biology Olympiad or does labs/dissections and guest talks.
targetAudience: Students curious about biology/life sciences who want hands-on lab experience or want to compete academically in the subject.
detailedDescription: Biology Club goes beyond the classroom curriculum with hands-on labs, dissections, and talks from guest speakers in life-science fields. Many members prepare for national competitions like the USA Biology Olympiad, making it a strong fit for students who want a deeper, more independent dive into biology than regular coursework allows.
interests: Curious about the human body and genetics

name: Chess Club
description: Competitive and casual chess; players compete in team/individual tournaments.
targetAudience: Anyone who enjoys chess, from beginners to tournament-level players.
detailedDescription: Chess Club welcomes both players who just want to play casually after school and those chasing competitive tournament results. Members compete individually and as a team against other schools, with plenty of time to just play and improve in between.

name: Debate
description: Formal argumentation in formats like Lincoln-Douglas, Public Forum, or Policy. Research-heavy, competes at MSHSL tournaments.
targetAudience: Students who enjoy research, argumentation, and public speaking under pressure.
detailedDescription: Debate is a research-heavy competitive speech activity where students argue assigned resolutions in formats like Lincoln-Douglas (one-on-one value debate), Public Forum (team-based current-events debate), and Policy (evidence-intensive team debate). Members compete at MSHSL-sanctioned tournaments throughout the season.

name: Future Problem-Solvers
description: Part of Future Problem Solving Program International. Students apply a 6-step process to "future scene" scenarios on global topics (climate, tech, etc.), competing state → international. Combines research, creative writing, and skit performance.
targetAudience: Students who like creative problem-solving, research, writing, and a bit of performance.
detailedDescription: Part of Future Problem Solving Program International, this club has students apply a structured 6-step problem-solving process to hypothetical 'future scene' scenarios covering topics like climate change and emerging technology. It blends research, creative writing, and skit performance, with top teams advancing from state competition to the international finals.
interests: Cares about global issues like climate, tech, and society
Interested in policy, consulting, or social impact

name: Math Team
description: Timed individual and team math competitions (e.g., Minnesota State High School Math League).
targetAudience: Students who enjoy math and want to test their skills competitively.
detailedDescription: Math Team trains for and competes in timed problem-solving contests such as the Minnesota State High School Math League, testing speed and accuracy across a range of math topics both individually and as a team.
interests: Interested in engineering, computer science, finance, or actuarial work

name: Mock Trial
description: Simulated courtroom trials; students play attorneys and witnesses, judged on legal argument and presentation.
targetAudience: Students interested in law, public speaking, and improvisation.
detailedDescription: Mock Trial recreates courtroom proceedings, with students preparing and arguing both sides of a fictional case as attorneys or playing witness roles. Teams are judged on legal reasoning, courtroom presentation, and improvisational skill, competing against other schools' teams.
interests: Has a dramatic or theatrical streak
Likes debate but wants more structure

name: Model United Nations
description: Students role-play as country delegates, debating global issues and drafting resolutions in simulated UN committees.
targetAudience: Students interested in global affairs, diplomacy, and debate.
detailedDescription: Model UN has students represent assigned countries in simulated United Nations committees, debating real global issues, negotiating with other delegates, and drafting formal resolutions. It's a mix of research, diplomacy, and public speaking.
interests: Interested in international relations and diplomacy
Interested in foreign service, law, or policy

name: Science Bowl
description: Fast-paced, buzzer-based Q&A quiz competition (DOE-sponsored) across physical science, math, biology, earth science. Quick-recall format.
targetAudience: Students who love science trivia and quick recall under pressure.
detailedDescription: Science Bowl is a DOE-sponsored, buzzer-based quiz competition testing quick recall across physical science, math, biology, and earth science. It's a fast-paced format that rewards breadth of knowledge and speed.
interests: Strong across multiple sciences and math

name: Science Olympiad
description: Team-based competition with ~23 hands-on and knowledge events (building devices, lab practicals). Broader and more project/build-oriented than Science Bowl.
targetAudience: Students who like building things and hands-on science, not just quizzing.
detailedDescription: Science Olympiad is a broad, project-oriented team competition spanning around 23 events -- some are knowledge tests, others require building and testing devices beforehand. It's more hands-on and build-focused than Science Bowl, rewarding both engineering skill and science knowledge.
interests: Likes variety, mixing knowledge events with building events

name: Quiz Bowl
description: General-knowledge buzzer trivia across all academic subjects and pop culture.
targetAudience: Students who love trivia and general knowledge.
detailedDescription: Quiz Bowl is a fast buzzer-based trivia competition covering everything from academic subjects to pop culture, rewarding broad general knowledge and quick recall.
interests: Enjoys both pop culture and academics

name: Speech
description: Individual competitive public speaking in categories like extemporaneous, original oratory, and dramatic interpretation.
targetAudience: Students who enjoy public speaking or performance and want individual competition.
detailedDescription: Speech is an individual competitive speaking activity with categories ranging from extemporaneous speaking (impromptu current events) to original oratory and dramatic/humorous interpretation. Competitors are judged on delivery, content, and performance.
interests: Interested in broadcasting, law, teaching, or acting
Wants to build confidence and communication skills

name: Business Professionals of America (BPA)
description: Business, IT, office administration, and finance skills; competes in technical/leadership events.
targetAudience: Students interested in business, office/IT skills, or finance careers.
detailedDescription: BPA is a Career and Technical Student Organization focused on business, information technology, office administration, and finance skills. Members prepare for technical and leadership competitive events, building career-ready skills in professional and IT-adjacent fields.
interests: Interested in business, IT, or finance
Has corporate or professional career goals

name: DECA
description: Marketing, finance, hospitality, management, and entrepreneurship. Role-play case studies and business plan competitions. Overlaps somewhat with BPA but is marketing/entrepreneurship-focused rather than office/IT-focused.
targetAudience: Students interested in marketing, entrepreneurship, or business strategy.
detailedDescription: DECA prepares students for careers in marketing, finance, hospitality, and entrepreneurship through role-play case-study competitions and business plan events. It overlaps with BPA but leans more toward marketing and entrepreneurship than office/IT skills.
interests: Interested in business or finance majors

name: Esports
description: Competitive organized video gaming (titles vary by season/league). Advisor listed as TBD.
targetAudience: Students who want to compete in video games at a school-sponsored, team level.
detailedDescription: Esports is Wayzata's competitive gaming team, playing organized matches against other schools with titles varying by season and league. Advisor is currently listed as TBD.
interests: Interested in gaming, streaming, or tech
Wants a competitive outlet that is not traditional sports

name: HOSA Future Health Professionals
description: For students interested in healthcare/medicine; competitions in clinical and health-knowledge events.
targetAudience: Students considering a career in healthcare or medicine.
detailedDescription: HOSA is a CTSO for students interested in healthcare and medicine, offering competitive events in clinical skills and health knowledge alongside opportunities to explore medical career paths.
interests: Future doctors, nurses, EMTs, dentists, or therapists
Interested in medicine and healthcare careers
Wants exposure to the healthcare field

name: Robotics
description: Design, build, and program robots for VEX Robotics competitions.
targetAudience: Students interested in engineering, coding, and hands-on building.
detailedDescription: Robotics has students design, build, and program robots to compete in VEX Robotics competitions, combining engineering, coding, and teamwork under tight build-season deadlines.
interests: Interested in engineering or computer science
Interested in mechanical, electrical, or software careers

name: SkillsUSA
description: Skilled trades and technical/service careers (welding, automotive, construction, etc.); competes in hands-on trade contests.
targetAudience: Students interested in trades and technical/vocational careers.
detailedDescription: SkillsUSA prepares students for skilled trade and technical service careers such as welding, automotive repair, and construction, with hands-on trade-specific competitive events.
interests: Interested in skilled trades like welding, automotive, construction, or electrical

name: Super Mileage Team
description: Engineering-focused: students build ultra-fuel-efficient vehicles and compete on miles-per-gallon. Advisor TBD.
targetAudience: Students interested in mechanical engineering and hands-on vehicle building.
detailedDescription: Super Mileage Team is an engineering-focused club where students design and build ultra-fuel-efficient vehicles, competing against other schools on fuel economy. Advisor is currently listed as TBD.
interests: Interested in mechanical or automotive engineering

name: Trap & Skeet Club
description: Competitive clay-target shooting sports (typically via the USA Clay Target League).
targetAudience: Students interested in shooting sports.
detailedDescription: Trap & Skeet Club competes in clay-target shooting sports, typically through the USA Clay Target League, combining precision and individual skill in a team-scored format.

name: Chinese Club
description: Chinese language and cultural activities.
targetAudience: Students learning Chinese or interested in Chinese culture.
detailedDescription: Chinese Club combines language practice with cultural activities, giving students a chance to learn about and celebrate Chinese culture together.
interests: Interested in Chinese language and culture
Interested in international business or travel

name: French Club
description: French language and culture.
targetAudience: Students learning French or interested in French culture.
detailedDescription: French Club gives students a low-pressure space to practice French and take part in cultural activities and events tied to French-speaking cultures.
interests: Interested in French language and culture
Interested in travel or international topics

name: German Club
description: German language and culture.
targetAudience: Students learning German or interested in German culture.
detailedDescription: German Club gives students a low-pressure space to practice German and take part in cultural activities and events tied to German-speaking cultures.
interests: Interested in German language and culture

name: International Club
description: Celebrates global cultures broadly; usually food, cultural events, and cross-cultural exchange.
targetAudience: Students interested in exploring and celebrating cultures from around the world.
detailedDescription: International Club takes a broad approach to celebrating cultures from around the world, organizing food-centered events, cultural showcases, and opportunities for cross-cultural exchange among students.
interests: Interested in global food and traditions
Connects well with international and exchange students

name: Spanish Club
description: Spanish language and culture.
targetAudience: Students learning Spanish or interested in Spanish-speaking cultures.
detailedDescription: Spanish Club gives students a space to practice Spanish and take part in cultural activities and events tied to Spanish-speaking cultures.
interests: Interested in Spanish language and culture
Plans to use Spanish in a career such as healthcare, education, or business

name: Club Unified Students
description: Almost certainly tied to Special Olympics Unified Champion Schools: pairs students with and without intellectual disabilities in shared activities to promote inclusion.
targetAudience: Students who want to build an inclusive community, including students with and without disabilities.
detailedDescription: Likely tied to Special Olympics Unified Champion Schools, this club pairs students with and without intellectual disabilities in shared social and athletic activities, building inclusion and friendship across the student body. Exact program details unconfirmed -- worth checking with the advisor.
interests: Enjoys working with peers of all abilities
Interested in special education, therapy, or social work

name: Link Crew
description: A national transition program where upperclassmen mentor incoming freshmen to ease the move into high school.
targetAudience: Upperclassmen who want to mentor, and by extension, all incoming freshmen.
detailedDescription: Link Crew is a national transition program where trained upperclassmen mentor incoming freshmen, helping them navigate the move to high school socially and academically.
interests: An upperclassman who likes helping younger students

name: National Honor Society
description: Recognizes academic achievement; requires service hours and upholds scholarship, leadership, service, and character.
targetAudience: High-achieving students who want to build a strong service and leadership record.
detailedDescription: National Honor Society recognizes students for strong academics while requiring ongoing community service hours and involvement, built around the four pillars of scholarship, leadership, service, and character.
interests: Wants recognition and a college resume boost

name: Student Council
description: Elected student government; plans events, represents the student body, organizes school spirit activities.
targetAudience: Students who want to be involved in school leadership and event planning.
detailedDescription: Student Council is the school's elected student government, planning events, representing student interests to administration, and organizing school spirit activities throughout the year.
interests: Wants a voice in the school
Interested in management, politics, or organizing

name: Volunteer Club
description: Organizes community service and volunteer opportunities.
targetAudience: Students who want an easy, flexible way to get involved in community service.
detailedDescription: Volunteer Club connects students with community service and volunteer opportunities throughout the year, making it easy to rack up service hours while giving back locally.
interests: Wants a flexible, low-commitment service option

name: Band
advisor: Dave Elmhirst, Don Krubsack, Dan Tewalt
description: Instrumental ensembles (concert, marching, jazz, etc.). Three advisors suggests multiple bands.
targetAudience: Instrumentalists of varying experience levels.
detailedDescription: Band covers a range of instrumental ensembles -- concert, marching, and jazz among them -- with multiple advisors reflecting the range of groups offered.
interests: Plays a wind, brass, or percussion instrument
Likes performing and working in an ensemble
Full of school spirit, especially for marching

name: Choirs
description: Vocal ensembles.
targetAudience: Students who enjoy singing.
detailedDescription: Choirs offers multiple vocal ensembles for students who want to sing, ranging in style and skill level.

name: Dance Club
description: Choreography and performance.
targetAudience: Students interested in dance and performance.
detailedDescription: Dance Club focuses on choreography and performance, giving members a creative outlet through movement.

name: Drama Club and Theatre
description: Stage productions; acting and tech/production.
targetAudience: Students interested in acting, directing, or technical theater production.
detailedDescription: Drama Club and Theatre puts on stage productions, with roles both on stage (acting) and behind the scenes (tech and production), covering the full range of what it takes to put on a show.
interests: Also fits students who like backstage tech such as lighting, sets, and costumes

name: Orchestras
description: String/full orchestral ensembles.
targetAudience: String and orchestral instrumentalists.
detailedDescription: Orchestras offers string and full-orchestra ensembles for instrumentalists who want to perform classical and contemporary repertoire together.

name: Art Club
description: Visual arts creation, projects, possibly exhibitions.
targetAudience: Students interested in visual art of any medium or skill level.
detailedDescription: Art Club gives students an open space to work on visual art projects, experiment with new mediums, and potentially showcase their work in exhibitions.
interests: Interested in art or design careers

name: Creative Writing Club / The Voice Literary Magazine
description: Creative writing plus producing the school's literary magazine (student poetry/prose/art).
targetAudience: Students who like to write creatively, or want to help produce a literary publication.
detailedDescription: This club combines creative writing workshopping with producing The Voice, the school's literary magazine featuring student poetry, prose, and art.
interests: Likes publishing and sharing their work
Interested in becoming a writer or editor

name: Trojan Tribune Journalism Club
description: Student newspaper; reporting, writing, editing school news.
targetAudience: Students interested in journalism, reporting, or writing.
detailedDescription: Trojan Tribune Journalism Club runs the school newspaper, with students reporting, writing, and editing news stories about the school and community.
interests: Interested in journalism, media, or communications

name: Wayako Yearbook
description: Produces the annual yearbook (photography, layout, writing).
targetAudience: Students interested in photography, design, or writing/documentation.
detailedDescription: Wayako Yearbook is responsible for producing the school's annual yearbook, covering photography, page layout and design, and writing captions and features.
interests: Interested in design or media careers
